name: Chin tuck trainer

lead: A chin tuck trainer is a device, often an inflatable pad or strap with resistance, that gives feedback or load during chin-tuck (craniocervical flexion) exercises. The exercise draws the head back over the shoulders.
It is used to address forward head posture, which looks like a protruding chin and a weaker jawline profile in photos.

paras: Chin tucks recruit the deep neck flexors, which stabilize the upper cervical spine, and stretch the short extensors at the base of the skull. Systematic reviews report that exercise can improve the craniovertebral angle and neuromuscular coordination, with less consistent benefits on strength and pain; certainty of evidence is low to moderate.

The exercise is low risk, but overdoing it can strain neck muscles or cause headaches. The device adds little beyond the plain exercise, which can be done with no equipment, so claims that a trainer is needed are overstated. Posture improvements require repeated practice and are partial, not guaranteed.
